acts: If detained: ask why, tell family, get a lawyer · NALSA 15100
Check the date and the source first

cases.name: Umar Khalid
cases.status: Delhi High Court rejected his bail for the third time on 30 Sep 2026; trial not begun. Police called fresh bail pleas premature

cases.name: Sharjeel Imam
cases.status: Bail rejected by Delhi High Court 30 Sep 2026. A 7-day interim bail ended 10 Oct; a court found a media-contact breach but did not cancel it. Police called it misuse of liberty

cases.name: Srishti Gupta
cases.status: No bail in 2 of 11 cases. Her bail order notes she was not at the site of the violence; police chargesheet calls her a key conspirator

cases.name: Satyam Verma
cases.law: NSA (order 12 May 2026) plus Noida protest FIRs
cases.status: Journalist still held under NSA despite bail in one case on 15 Sep. Allahabad High Court reserved its verdict on his NSA challenge on 8 Oct; state's arguments not reported

cases.name: Pranab Doley
cases.status: Held under NSA after getting bail. High Court hearings on his challenge keep being adjourned as the state seeks time to file its affidavit. Govt cites public order

cases.name: Siang dam protesters (4)
cases.status: Still held. A 23 Oct bandh demanding their release ended in arson in Pasighat. District says detainees must make representations; CM has offered talks

cases.name: Dawit Isaak
cases.status: Journalist held incommunicado 25 years; whereabouts and health unknown. Eritrea's president has said there will be no trial and no release

cases.name: Abdulhadi Al-Khawaja
cases.status: Human rights defender in Jau Prison; rights groups urged France's president to press for his release (16 Oct). No Bahraini government response reported

cases.name: Osman Kavala
cases.status: Istanbul court refused release and retrial (14 Oct) despite a European Court of Human Rights ruling; government says courts are independent and the case is not political

cases.name: Jimmy Lai
cases.status: Serving 20 years, aged 78. UK urged release (22 Oct); Hong Kong rejected this, saying he was not tried for his political views

cases.name: Aung San Suu Kyi
cases.status: Under house arrest in Naypyidaw; spoke to her son by phone on 22 Oct, the first time in five years. Government rejects calls for release

cases.name: Imran Aliyev
cases.law: Smuggling, money laundering, tax evasion, forgery charges
cases.status: Meclis.info founder; prosecutors sought 12 years (20 Oct), verdict expected 3 Nov. Authorities say outlets broke foreign-grant rules

cases.name: Dr Hussam Abu Safiya
cases.law: Unlawful Combatants Law; no charge, no trial
cases.status: Hospital director; lawyer reports abuse in custody. Israel alleges Hamas links, which family and lawyers deny

cases.name: Detainees held by the RSF
cases.countcap: held in El Geneina, doctors say
cases.status: Amnesty reports torture, forced labour and ransom-for-release in El Fasher; doctors report food shortages and deaths in El Geneina. RSF did not respond

cases.name: Najmeh Amini
cases.law: Death sentence for blasphemy; 12.5 years on security charges
cases.status: 23-year-old student held in Mashhad Central Prison, sentenced to death over social media posts. No official statement reported

items.headline: Pasighat under gathering ban after dam unrest
items.text: After Friday night's arson in Pasighat, police detained five youths for questioning and barred gatherings of more than five people from Saturday evening; activists including lawyer Ebo Mili surrendered, saying the bandh was peaceful. Chief Minister Pema Khandu offered talks, saying the government's doors are open.

items.headline: Six, including four women, held under UAPA
items.text: Bandipora police announced on Saturday the arrest of six people, four of them women, under the anti-terror UAPA. Police allege a network linked to the banned Ittihad-ul-Muslimeen spread separatist ideology and received about ₹8 lakh; no response from the accused or their families was reported.

items.headline: CBI books seven police over custodial death
items.text: On the High Court's direction, the CBI has booked seven people, including a suspended inspector, over the death of 25-year-old Gade Sai Krishna. His mother alleges he was illegally detained and tortured at Krishnalanka police station and his body burned; the accused have not been tried.

items.headline: Imphal sit-in against any division of Manipur
items.text: Five civil society groups led by AMUCO held a sit-in in Imphal East on Saturday, starting a statewide agitation against any administrative division of Manipur; their six demands include repeal of AFSPA and rehabilitation of displaced people. No police action or government response was reported.

items.headline: 410,000–800,000 march in France; ~1,000 arrested
items.text: Between 410,000 (interior ministry) and about 800,000 (organisers) marched on Saturday over schools and living costs. Police used tear gas in Paris, Lyon, Nantes and other cities, where some protests were banned. The interior minister reported nearly 1,000 arrests and "an extremely elevated level of violence."

items.headline: Families displaced in Hebron military operation
items.text: About 250 families, almost 1,200 people according to Hebron's municipality, were displaced as Israeli forces entered Hebron on Saturday after two soldiers were killed; demolitions began near the attack site. The military says it is dismantling "terrorist infrastructure" and removing structures that pose a security threat.

items.place: Beit Lahia and Gaza City, Gaza
items.headline: Two killed in Gaza despite ceasefire
items.text: A woman was shot dead in Beit Lahia and a man killed by a drone strike in Gaza City on Saturday, medical sources said. Gaza's Health Ministry says 1,547 people have been killed since the ceasefire began. No Israeli military comment on these deaths was reported.

items.headline: Drone strikes; ex-detainees describe torture
items.text: Drones residents attribute to the army hit El Fasher's market on Thursday, killing civilians and fighters, Darfur24 reports. Amnesty says fewer than 70,000 people remain a year after the RSF took the city and former detainees describe torture. Neither the army nor the RSF has responded.

focus.title: The fight over the Siang dam
focus.dek: Villages along the Siang oppose an 11,000 MW dam that would submerge 27 villages. Four villagers are held under an anti-terror law, a bandh on 23 October ended in tear gas and arson, and on 24 October Pasighat came under prohibitory orders as the chief minister offered talks.
focus.alt: A wide, calm river between forested hills, with tall grass in the foreground.
